newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares ease, off lows in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares ease, off lows in thin trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares slipped 0.84 percent lower in depressed trade on Monday amid persistent cash shortage and negative sentiment, brokers said.
Part of the early losses was recovered on minor selective buying in the afternoon, but trade remained in a narrow band, they said.

The IMKB-100 closed at 62,904.83, down 534.01 points from Friday after moving between 62,618 and 63,438. Trade volume plunged to 3.4 trillion lira, nearing the 1996 low of 2.7 trillion on July 30, after Friday's 5.6 trillion.
"The index has firm support at 62,500. It did not fall much although negative developments undermining the market follow one another," said Haydar Haydaroglu from Halkbank.
"There is even a stronger support at 61,500, so the market is trying to bottom out at the current levels. Selective activity emerged to overcome the squeeze," he added.

Brokers said the market was unnerved by weekend incidents in Cyprus and ongoing fighting in northern Iraq as well as international opposition, particularly from Arab countries to a Turkish plan to set up a security zone there to prevent infiltrations by Kurdish rebels.
A Turkish Cypriot soldier was killed and another was seriously wounded on Sunday when shots were fired at their posts near the U.N.-patrolled buffer zone.
The market had lost 1.7 percent last week mainly due to fighting in northern Iraq which was followed by U.S. missile strikes on military targets in southern Iraq.

Brokers said a strong dollar also discouraged market players. The lira weakened sharply to 87,940 against the dollar from Friday's 87,350 close due to a higher dollar/mark parity and despite money shortage.

The 85-share industrial index fell 0.88 percent to 69,065.8 and the 15-share financial index eased 0.73 percent to 55,600.31. Of the 219 shares traded, losers outdid gainers sharply by 121 to 39 and 59 ended unchanged.
Actives were led by partially privatised flat steel giant Eregli, steady at 8,000 lira and consumer electronics producer Raks Elektrikli Ev Aletleri, up 1,000 lira at 29,500.
